quick_skim.title: Generative Text Modelling and Language-Guided Visual Attention for Deciphering Palimpsests
quick_skim.abstract: Recovering obscured text in palimpsests, i.e. the manuscripts where the original writing (under-text) was erased and overwritten for reuse, is vital for preserving lost information. Due to the nature of the material, such a task can be highly challenging and time-consuming. This paper presents an approach towards automated palimpsest handwritten text modeling for under-text recovery. We investigate generative models, including Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) and diffusion models, and design a custom denoising diffusion model that learns structured noise patterns to reconstruct the under-text. The recovered text is subsequently processed by a fine-tuned, attention-based handwritten text recognition network. Furthermore, we investigate a language-guided recognition framework that leverages textual class descriptions as informative priors, enabling the text recognition model to distinguish meaningful features from noise. This is achieved by grounding task-specific descriptions, phrased in words or sentences, through visual attention maps generated by pretrained vision-language models like CLIP (Contrastive Language-Image Pre-training). To facilitate future research and benchmarking, we release new datasets for synthetic palimpsests (currently scarce), CLIP-compatible text descriptions, and pre-trained models with code.

quick_skim.llm_tldr_en: The paper recovers erased under-text in palimpsest manuscripts using generative diffusion models, then recognizes the recovered handwriting with a fine-tuned attention-based HTR network.
quick_skim.llm_tldr_cn: 该文针对重写本手稿中原文字被擦除覆盖、人工恢复耗时困难的问题，探索GAN与扩散模型并设计定制去噪扩散模型学习结构化噪声以重建底层文字。重建文本随后交由微调的注意力式手写文本识别网络处理。该流程将生成式复原与离线手写识别结合，展示了在文化遗产手稿场景中自动恢复与识别的可行路径。
